minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard the facilities director's FY26 capital requests; no funding decisions were made, only follow-ups requested.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the facilities director present the FY26 capital list (public safety second floor design, senior center parking and flooring, Town Hall HVAC and windows, library HVAC design, teen center flooring, MCN Park survey, Marshall Pond weeds) plus out-year items. Members pushed for a real five-year plan, removal of never-to-be-done items, a backlog and funding-gap view, and a corrected spreadsheet and deck. The only vote was approving three sets of prior minutes, then adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Chair opened public comment at the start; no one spoke.
Chair asked for public comment at the close; none offered.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of the 7/10, 7/31 and 10/9 meetings as presented

budget_items.what_was_said: Slide typo corrected; cost should read 25,000, not 35,000.
Director guessed a design cost for the second-floor build-out; the number was on a slide but not shown in the version viewed.
Figure covers civil engineering items (test pits, permitting, conceptual plans, survey, estimator); the next phase figure is a carryover shot in the dark and likely low.
A member said a scanner for odd-format land use documents could cost tens of thousands.
Town Hall HVAC and windows may be grant-eligible; one more round up to a cap, then a per-year cap.
Design/engineering questioned; roof-unit design estimate and ongoing repair costs described; design would let projects be phased.
Director doubts justifying roof money for a section of TCP given the school may leave.
A member worried a historic-style requirement could double a window cost.
Full hydro-raking estimate was too large; proposal is a limited start covering about a fifth of the work.
Prior estimator quote was higher than the current one; window material alone nearly consumes the capital project.
Gas bill exceeds revenue; abatement cost grows each year of delay.

decisions.decision: Facilities director to send a corrected slide deck (teen center flooring figure and slide order) this week.
Director to supply the full spreadsheet with updated numbers, an updated deck, and flagged placeholder estimates.
Director to put together an overview of funding gaps; committee also wants a backlog and completion projection for already-funded projects.
Next meeting November 4 (DPW and fire scheduled); further presentations likely by Zoom, with at least two more meetings before early December.
Unlikely items such as Brooks house projects to be moved into a separate bucket rather than the five-year plan.
Chair to schedule the IT presentation and speak with the presenter first to align format.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee made no funding decisions; it heard the facilities director present the FY26 capital requests and out-year items.
The only vote was approval of three sets of prior minutes, followed by adjournment.
Members asked the director for a full updated spreadsheet, a corrected deck, flagged placeholder estimates, and an overview of funding gaps.
Members also asked that items unlikely to be done be moved into a separate bucket, outside a real five-year plan.
The next meeting is November 4, with DPW and fire scheduled, and at least two more meetings before early December.

why_it_matters: These FY26 capital requests, such as Town Hall HVAC and windows, library HVAC design, and senior center parking, are the list that later reaches Town Meeting for funding votes, and several estimates were still described as placeholders or likely low.

reconciliation.summary: Neither record has a vote or transfer, and the figures the two share mostly agree. Our minutes record many more budget items (public safety design, TCP roof, Town Hall windows, Ritter, TCP carrying costs, contingency) than the official minutes print. The one substantive difference is the meeting schedule: we heard further meetings before early December, and the official minutes say all presentations are to finish before Christmas.
